spec_match.rationale: The getter-on-the-dictionary probe tests the exact new PositionOptions member without needing a permission grant, and the comparison table exercises getCurrentPosition with accuracyMode precise vs approximate and reads back the accuracy radius the spec change is about.

interactive.rationale: Real controls run the support probe and the two live position requests, populate a results table with coordinates, radius and time-to-fix, and a privacy toggle rounds displayed coordinates.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card promises calling the real API in both modes plus a support probe that can tell honoured from ignored — exactly what the page ships.

edge_cases.rationale: Handles missing geolocation, permission denied (with copy calling it a legitimate outcome), unavailable and timeout error codes, and the silently-dropped-member case, which is precisely what this 141 build exhibits.

references.rationale: See-also cites https://chromestatus.com/feature/5143609755828224 and the w3c/geolocation spec PR.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite is genuinely contract-level — the getter-read probe, the WebIDL enum TypeError negative, default-precise compatibility and the permission query; on Chromium 141 it ran 6 pass / 2 fail with exactly the two accuracyMode assertions failing, the correct pre-157 split.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): desktop and true-360 mobile screenshots read, DOM dumped, console clean ('[approx-geo:probe] ready'), and the /conformance/ route plus in-page support panel observed at 6 pass / 2 fail — but the probe and request buttons are click-driven (and a real fix needs a permission grant headless auto-denies), so those paths are judged from the wiring.

telemetry_health.rationale: showcaseTelemetry?.assert covers the member-read result, successful fixes per mode with radius and timing, and each failure code; load is console-clean.

design_system.rationale: Variables and button overrides are correct throughout, but the amber 'Not run yet.' verdict (--accent-amber #b87b00 on --bg-paper, ~3.6:1) and the emerald ok-verdict (~3.7:1 on stone) both miss WCAG AA 4.5:1 for normal-size bold text.

accessibility.rationale: Probe and comparison outcomes land in aria-live=polite outputs, the results table has a caption and column headers, the rounding checkbox sits inside its label, and verdict icons are aria-hidden with text equivalents.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: At a true 360px viewport the five-column mono results table forces the whole 'Compare the two modes' stage wider than the viewport, and because the body clips horizontal overflow the privacy note text, the 'Request approximate' button and the rounding-checkbox label are visibly cut off — desktop (1280px) is clean.

openQuestions.title: Results table overflows and clips the compare stage at mobile width
openQuestions.detail: The 360px capture shows the note ('This asks for your real location. Chr…'), the Request approximate button and the checkbox label clipped at the right edge: the table's five mono columns set a min-content width beyond 360px, the grid stage stretches to it, and body overflow-x:hidden crops everything in that stage. Wrap the table in its own overflow-x:auto container (so only the table scrolls) or collapse it to stacked rows at narrow widths, then re-verify at 360px — this is the mobile+desktop parity invariant's core case (clipped controls/text).

openQuestions.title: Amber and emerald verdict colours miss WCAG AA
openQuestions.detail: The .unknown verdict uses --accent-amber (#b87b00) on the white stage (~3.6:1) and the .ok verdict uses --accent-emerald (#0a8f5c) on stone (~3.7:1); both are below 4.5:1 at their normal text size. The rose fail state passes. This is the recurring shared-palette shortfall — worth a single palette-level decision rather than per-page hexes.

summary: A genuinely well-designed probe page: the getter-on-PositionOptions trick distinguishes 'option honoured' from 'option silently dropped' with no permission prompt, and the mode-comparison table reads back real radii with a privacy-rounding control. Verified with headless Chromium 141 at http://localhost:3000/v157/approximate-geolocation/accuracy-mode-probe/ (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp; desktop + true-360 mobile screenshots including a full-height mobile capture, DOM dump, clean console; feature /conformance/ route and the in-page support panel both at 6 pass / 2 fail — the two accuracyMode assertions failing is the correct pre-157 result on this build). Buttons could not be clicked headlessly. The one real defect is responsive: the results table forces the whole compare stage past 360px and the body's overflow clip cuts off the note, a button and the checkbox label on mobile.
